summary: A lawyer asks Jesus how to inherit eternal life, then who his neighbor is. Jesus answers with a story of a Samaritan who stops to save a wounded stranger.
key_insight: The lawyer asked, “And who is my neighbor?” Jesus ended by asking which of the three “was neighbor to him.” The question moved from who deserves my love to whether I will show it.
story: A lawyer, an expert in the law of Moses, stood up to test Jesus: “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?” Jesus asked him, “What is written in the law? What is your reading of it?” The lawyer answered with two commands: “You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind,” and love “your neighbor as yourself.” “You have answered rightly,” Jesus said; “do this and you will live.”
But the lawyer, wanting to justify himself, asked, “And who is my neighbor?”

Jesus answered with a story. “A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves.” They stripped him, beat him and left him half dead. By chance a priest came down that road; when he saw the man, he passed by on the other side. A Levite came to the place, looked at him, and passed by on the other side as well.

“But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was. And when he saw him, he had compassion.” He went to the man and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn and took care of him. The next day he gave the innkeeper two denarii and said, “Take care of him; and whatever more you spend, when I come again, I will repay you.”
Then Jesus asked, “So which of these three do you think was neighbor to him who fell among the thieves?” The lawyer said, “He who showed mercy on him.” Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”

scene.label: The Jericho road
scene.text: The road from Jerusalem to Jericho falls more than 3,000 feet in about seventeen miles through barren, rocky hills, and its bends and caves made it a known haunt of robbers. Part of it passed the Ascent of Adummim (Joshua 15:7), a name that means red.

scene.label: Priest and Levite
scene.text: Priests offered the sacrifices; Levites assisted them in the temple. The law kept priests from touching the dead (Leviticus 21:1), and the man looked “half dead.” But Jesus gives no reason for their passing by, and the story does not need one.

scene.label: Samaritans
scene.text: Jews and Samaritans had been hostile for centuries. Samaritans descended in part from peoples the Assyrians settled in the land (2 Kings 17:24), and the Jewish ruler John Hyrcanus had destroyed their temple on Mount Gerizim more than a century before. As John notes, “Jews have no dealings with Samaritans” (John 4:9).

scene.label: Oil, wine and two denarii
scene.text: Wine was used to clean wounds and oil to soothe them (compare Isaiah 1:6). Two denarii were two days’ wages for a laborer (Matthew 20:2), probably enough to keep the man at the inn for some days.

scene.label: Who counts as a neighbor
scene.text: Leviticus 19:18 commands love for “your neighbor as yourself,” and the same chapter tells Israel to love the stranger as themselves (19:34). Many in Jesus’ day drew the circle of “neighbor” around fellow Israelites.

witnesses.luke: Only Luke records this parable, and it fits his care for outsiders: the hero is a Samaritan. Luke uses the same word for the Samaritan’s compassion that he uses for Jesus at the funeral in Nain (Luke 7:13). A similar exchange about the great commandments comes in Holy Week (Mark 12:28–34), but there Jesus gives the answer; here the lawyer does.

seeing.reveals: Jesus knows the law better than its experts and will not let it shrink into a definition. He answers a test with a story that makes a despised Samaritan the picture of the mercy God commands.
seeing.living: The lawyer wanted to know where his duty ended. Jesus told him to go and do what the Samaritan did: stop, and spend his own time and money on a stranger in need. The person lying in your road may be someone you were raised to avoid.
seeing.ponder: Whom have you quietly placed outside the circle of people you must love?

preaching.big_idea: The question is not who my neighbor is, but whether I will be one.
outline: A question looking for a limit (29)
preaching.watch_for: The lawyer asks two questions (vv. 25, 29), and Jesus answers each with a question of His own (vv. 26, 36). Both exchanges end with a command to act: “do this” (v. 28) and “Go and do likewise” (v. 37).
